## What Is a Center for American Progress Internship?


A Center for American Progress internship is a placement in one department of American Progress, the Washington, DC policy organization that is actually two nonprofits: the Center for American Progress, a 501(c)(3) research institute, and the Center for American Progress Action Fund, a 501(c)(4) advocacy organization. The two share office space and employees, and the postings simply say "American Progress".


Interns work in teams such as Economic Policy, Health Policy, Digital Technology and Legal. The summer 2026 posting says Digital Engagement interns help with rapid-response video and social posts, Digital Technology interns clean data and build simple dashboards, and Rights and Justice interns monitor the Federal Register and summarize congressional hearings.


## When Do Center for American Progress Internship Applications Open for 2027–2028?


American Progress doesn't run one recruiting season. It posts internships term by term, each one "until the position is filled", so the lead time is short. American Progress has not published how far ahead of a term it posts.


The only expectation we can support is low confidence: summer 2027 postings around February to March 2027, based on when American Progress's own summer 2026 page (March 2026) and resume bank page (February 2026) were last updated. Spring 2027 postings have not been announced. In 2026 the organization also ran an Internship Resume Bank, where students submitted once to be considered for later openings. It is closed too.

### Why You Must Apply the Week Applications Open


The evidence points to rolling review. The summer 2026 announcement said it "will remain posted until the position is filled", with no closing date, and teams can stop reviewing once they have a pool. Nobody outside the organization knows how quickly a given posting fills, so the safe habit is to apply in the first days after one goes up.


The practical steps: bookmark the internships page, subscribe to the site's jobs updates, and draft a cover letter now. The Rights and Justice posting asked cover letters to say when you're available, what in the department's work interests you, and what policy areas you want to learn.

## Which Center for American Progress Internship Programs Should You Target?


American Progress doesn't run one named program. It places interns on policy, data, digital and legal teams, and has not published a department list on its live pages while no internship is open.


Area Focus Duration Key skills


Teams vary by term Policy research, data, digital content and legal support, depending on the posting Not published Read the skills listed in each posting


Current and past postings sit on the[American Progress internships page](https://www.americanprogress.org/about-us/internships/) . Departments can change from term to term, so read each posting for the teams hiring.


## What Are the Eligibility Requirements?


The summer 2026 posting set these rules. Check the live posting for any change.


• **Who:** "current undergraduate and graduate students and recent graduates of up to six months."


• **Degree level by team:** it varies. Rights and Justice asked for a master's or doctoral student or recent graduate, Structural Reform and Governance for a master's/doctoral student or a third- or fourth-year undergraduate, and Climate and Energy for at least one year into a degree.


• **Location:** on site in the Washington, DC office; the posting says it is not remote.


• **GPA, citizenship and work authorization:** not stated in the posting text we could read.


• **Values language:** several team descriptions list a commitment to progressive values or interest in progressive policy among the qualities sought. Read the posting and apply if it fits you.


### Is There a GPA Cutoff?


No GPA is published in the posting text, so there's no stated cutoff to clear. What the postings do set is degree level, which differs by team: a first-year undergraduate fits some departments and not others. Match your year to the team before you write the cover letter.


## What Skills Does the Center for American Progress Look For, and How Do You Build Them?


The postings list skills team by team rather than as one list. Research and writing come first everywhere. Quantitative teams add tools: Economic Policy and Health Policy name Excel, Stata and R, and Digital Technology names data visualization tools plus Excel and Google Sheets. Health Policy also names Word, PowerPoint and Outlook.


Three buckets: policy research and writing (briefs, fact sheets, hearing summaries), data work (cleaning, charts, dashboards), and digital content (clipping, captioning, social copy). Legal interns need legal research and an interest in nonprofit and election law.

## What Is the Center for American Progress Application and Interview Process Like?


The process is simple on paper and quiet in practice. The details below come from the summer 2026 posting.


1. **Pick a department.** Match your degree level to the team's stated requirement.


2. **Apply through the Paycom link** in that posting, or the resume bank when it is open, with a resume and cover letter.


3. **Write to the team.** Rights and Justice, for example, asked for availability, what interests you in its work and which policy areas you want to learn.


4. **Wait for contact.** The posting says "only those individuals whose qualifications match the current needs of this position will be considered applicants and will receive responses."


5. **Confirm you can be on site** in Washington for the full term before accepting.


No interview format or decision timeline is published.


### What Students on Reddit Say


Student discussion of American Progress internships is thin. The one usable thread, from r/DCInterns, has an applicant who had applied about two weeks earlier and hadn't heard back, which fits a posting that only replies to matches. We left the card box out rather than stretch one comment into consensus.


## How Do You Stand Out for a Center for American Progress Internship?


American Progress publishes no applicant count, acceptance rate or conversion rate, so there is nothing to benchmark against. What the postings do show is specificity: each team lists the tools and tasks it wants.


Three moves help. First, apply to a team, not to the organization, and name the issue area you've studied. Second, show a work sample that matches the tools in the posting, such as a chart built in Excel or a short brief. Third, check the live posting early and often, because roles stay up only until filled.


No official source ties interns to staff jobs. Entry-level research assistant roles exist, with a resume bank and one opening listing $55,000 to $63,250, but they aren't presented as an intern pipeline.

## FAQ


### Can I still apply for a summer 2026 Center for American Progress internship?


No. The summer 2026 posting now reads "This position is closed," and the Internship Resume Bank is closed too. As of October 16, 2026 no internship is open on American Progress's jobs page. The next likely posting is for summer 2027, expected around February to March 2027, though that is a low-confidence estimate.


### When do Center for American Progress internship applications open?


There is no fixed season. American Progress posts internships per term and keeps each up until filled. It has not announced 2027 dates. Its own summer 2026 and resume bank pages were last updated in March and February 2026, so summer 2027 postings are expected around February to March 2027, with low confidence.


### Are Center for American Progress internships paid?


American Progress has not published intern pay on its own live pages while no internship is open. Check the pay line on each posting on its internships page when summer 2027 roles go up, and confirm it before you plan your budget. The posting itself is the only source we would rely on for the hourly rate.


### What departments take Center for American Progress interns?


American Progress has not published a current department list on its live pages while no internship is open. Teams such as Economic Policy, Health Policy, Digital Technology and Legal have taken interns, and the list can change each term. Check the internships page and each posting for the teams hiring.


### Can I do a Center for American Progress internship remotely?


Not in the postings we read. The summer 2026 posting says the internship is on site at the Washington, DC office and is not a remote position. American Progress sets the work model per term, so confirm it in each new posting before you plan housing or a commute.


### Who is eligible for a Center for American Progress internship?


The summer 2026 posting invited current undergraduate and graduate students and recent graduates of up to six months. Degree level varies by team, from at least one year into a degree to a master's or doctoral student. Citizenship, GPA and work-authorization rules weren't stated in the posting text.


### What is the Center for American Progress internship resume bank?


It is a form where current students and recent graduates submit materials once to be considered for later internship openings. American Progress ran one in 2026 alongside department postings. It is closed on October 16, 2026, so watch the internships page for it to reopen.


### Is the Center for American Progress the same as its Action Fund?


They are two related nonprofits that share office space and employees: the Center for American Progress, a 501(c)(3) research institute, and the Center for American Progress Action Fund, a 501(c)(4). Their postings use the name American Progress, so read each posting to see which team you'd join.
